findings.title: Global graph occupancy is asserted by fixed arithmetic, not observed from the plane
findings.evidence: globalGraphOccupancy is decodedRows.length + 1 and globalCapacityRemaining is W0_MAX_EPOCH_VERTICES - decodedRows.length - 1 (fixture lines 366-367). The test then asserts globalGraphOccupancy === journalCount + 1 and globalCapacityRemaining === W0_MAX_EPOCH_VERTICES - globalGraphOccupancy (test lines 144-145), which restates the same formula. Production capacity is judged from registration.index.size (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3866, :6502, :6921); the fixture never observes that index, so the anchor's occupancy is a documented assumption (comment at line 365) rather than measured evidence. Measured values (1515/6677 legacy, 1497/6695 settlement) are far from the 8,192 ceiling, so pass/fail does not depend on the +1. No private counter is read, and the plan text itself states the anchor is counted, so this is weak evidence rather than a contract breach.
findings.violated_requirement: None violated. Plan lines 104652-104654 (distinguish journal rows from global graph occupancy including the anchor; do not read or invent private capacity counters) are satisfied nominally; flagged because the occupancy assertion is tautological with the fixture derivation.

findings.title: Historical legacy saturation case identity was retitled in GREEN; 'original W0 seven' is six historical identities plus one new companion
findings.evidence: The consumed historical reporter (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b-green-71bca5d5/retained-58/result.json) has numTotalTests 6, with the failing case titled 'caps one authenticated writer, counts fence/join vertices, preserves another writer and closes below global capacity'. The observation-only RED preserved that title (authored.patch). GREEN (w0-green.patch, test hunk at line 317-318) renamed it to 'caps one legacy-profile writer, rejects the reserved fence, counts the causal join, preserves another writer and closes below global capacity' and changed fenceCount 1 to 0, and added the settlement companion as the seventh case. The regression and isolated expected rosters (expected-roster.json lines 25/29, 999/1003) validate only the new titles. The change is recorded in the patch, GREEN handoff and plan checkpoint, so it is not silent, but checkpoint prose calling the current roster the 'original W0 seven' is imprecise for traceability back to the historical six-case identity.
findings.violated_requirement: None violated. Requirements.md 'No old assertion, case identity, timer, workload, or consumer may be silently dropped' is met because the retitle and assertion reconciliation are explicitly documented and authorized by the GREEN paragraph (plan lines 104624-104626); flagged as a documentation precision item only.

findings.title: Current-successor cold-input pin is supplied in source but its runtime necessity is not demonstrated
findings.evidence: GREEN supplies exactCanonicalPinnedGenesisBootstrapOperationBytes from the single validated originalBootstrap at both sites (lines 660 and 1041), and the observer records pinMatchesOriginal for both. Only the epoch-two site is asserted at runtime (tests/phase-6b-d110c-0b1-bounded-checkpoint-red.test.ts:146 expects exactly one 'epoch-two' entry). The current-successor site runs only through afterRepeatCloseFailure in tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1b/committed-issuance-recovery-contract.ts:178, whose controls already passed before the pin existed (GREEN retained run: 216/220 with no 0c1b failure). Production treats a supplied pin as an additional acceptance path rather than fail-closed on mismatch (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4837-4847 falls through to the historical path), so the 51-case pass shows the pin is compatible at that site, not that it is exercised. The consumer RED checkpoint (plan lines 104867-104870) explicitly accepted static-only coverage for this site.
findings.violated_requirement: None violated. Requirements.md 'Both actual cold-input construction sites must receive detached bytes from one validated original epoch-zero bootstrap' is met at source level for both sites; runtime evidence is asymmetric as the plan anticipated. A future control could assert the 'current-successor' observer entry when the failure-recovery lifecycle runs.
